frequency_question: How often do structural frictions successfully block or delay announced major unilateral tariffs before their effective date?
membership_rule: Includes explicitly announced, highly publicized tariff implementations or sector-specific executive tariff orders that faced imminent statutory, administrative, or legal structural friction within a defined pre-enactment window; excludes purely rhetorical trial balloons never formally scheduled or codified.

cases.name: Clinton EU-US banana war tariff escalation threats
Trump Section 232 steel and aluminum tariffs
Trump proposed Mexico tariff threat (migrant pressure)

provenance_note: claimed 8 hits but 7 of 9 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 9 named major executive tariff actions/threats with fixed impending deadlines or schedules; 8 proceeded to implementation despite friction.
known_gaps: Excludes minor administrative postponements under sub-cabinet level review.
validity_reason: Statutory frameworks like Section 232, Section 301, and IEEPA remain stable over multi-year presidential terms.
